source_decisions.source: Cadena et al., TRO 2016 SLAM survey
source_decisions.boundary: A survey organizes claims but does not certify one estimator or deployment policy.
First-order Gaussian uncertainty can fail for nonlinear or multimodal posteriors.

source_decisions.source: Nav2 current Concepts, REP-105 convention, and robot_localization docs
used_for: smooth local drift versus global jumps
source_decisions.boundary: Frame conventions and a package API do not validate source semantics, covariance, or observability.
The paper assumes practical independent Gaussian errors, correct pairwise matches and useful initialization; it is 2D stop-and-scan and excludes high-level map construction.

source_decisions.source: GTSAM factor graph tutorial and robust noise documentation
source_decisions.boundary: The library does not make a false measurement true or guarantee global convergence.

private_transfer_gate.scenario: Warehouse robot with wheel slip, biased timing, spinning-LiDAR deskew error, aisle degeneracy, correlated sensor fusion, false and true loop closures, concurrent path execution, and stale scene revision.
private_transfer_gate.publication_policy: Keep the integrated test private; expose every necessary insight through derivation, Viz, operational contract, or paper evidence boundary.

source_extraction.paper: Lu and Milios 1997, Globally Consistent Range Scan Alignment for Environment Mapping
mechanism_notes: Incremental scan-to-model integration becomes difficult to repair because local frames are permanently merged.
Nodes are scan poses; weak links come from odometry and strong links from overlapping pairwise scan matches.
Each relation contributes a covariance-weighted Mahalanobis energy; one pose is fixed because relative observations leave global reference unobservable.
The linear special case yields X=(H^T C^-1 H)^-1 H^T C^-1 D and covariance (H^T C^-1 H)^-1.

SE(2) pose relations are linearized around current estimates, solved globally, updated, and iterated; the paper reports four to five iterations to machine-accuracy convergence and more than 90 percent of correctable error removed in the first iteration.
Experiments use 13 simulated loop poses and 30 real scans with 84 matched-scan links; they show bounded corrected pose error and aligned scans, not production safety or modern runtime.

events.observed: Camera and perception articles both require an acquisition-time global sensor pose, while motion planning assumes a coherent versioned map.
events.inference: Localization and SLAM are the next missing physical-state dependency; a ROS 2 communication article would improve operations but would leave the central state-estimation assumption unexplained.
events.decision: Implement Robot Localization & SLAM before the deeper ROS 2 graph/QoS article.

verification.actual: The content spec now owns observation-to-pose-to-map-to-scene revision.

events.observed: Lu and Milios preserve local scans and relative uncertain relations, fix one reference pose, solve all pose variables, then iterate a linearized system.
events.inference: The durable teaching insight is reparability through provenance and global consistency, not merely the historical matrix formula.
events.decision: Use Lu and Milios as the paper spine and connect it explicitly to modern factor graphs and atomic downstream rebase.

verification.expected: Paper claim, evidence, assumptions, and modern boundary are separable
verification.actual: The source ledger and paper scope state each boundary before implementation.

events.observed: Definitions alone do not expose timestamp, correlation, degeneracy, false loop, or concurrent rebase failures.
events.inference: A hard test must combine multiple individually plausible sensor outputs with one high-impact global correction and an executing planner.

implementation_decisions: Choose localization and SLAM before ROS 2 graph/QoS because adjacent physical-state articles depended on an unexplained map-frame pose and revision.
Order sections by causal data flow rather than sensor or algorithm taxonomy.
Treat time, covariance, correlation, observability, gauge, loop robustness, and revision consistency as separate acceptance contracts.
Keep map global accuracy and odom local continuity in separate transforms instead of presenting a single corrected pose.
Teach front-end matches as uncertain constraints and back-end optimization as inference over those constraints, not truth creation.
Preserve raw scans/submaps and pose provenance so loop corrections remain repairable downstream.
Use semantic colors and restrained curves; red appears only for drift, outlier, stale revision, or violated invariant.
Put Korean operation rationale inside every display equation and move longer boundary explanations into FormulaNote.
Separate the 1997 paper's evidence from modern robust, sparse, incremental, and planner-transaction extensions.
